text:
Moritz Seider is playing almost 26 minutes a night for a Red Wings team that has won two of his last ten games, in a season already dominated by Dylan Larkin's refusal to play until he's traded. That's the backdrop, and it's not a kind one for a defenseman whose job is to carry everything.

His line reads 1 goal and 13 points in 23 games, seven on the power play, plus 63 blocked shots. Last season Evolving-Hockey had him 3rd among 215 defensemen in wins above replacement, at the 97th percentile for driving offense and 99th for suppressing it. This season the 5v5 numbers are flatter: Detroit takes 47% of the expected goals with him on, three points worse than without him.

Some of that is luck. He's shooting 2.4% against a likely 4 to 7%, and the team has scored about four goals fewer than its chances deserve with him out there. The points should come back toward the 1.5 per 60 we think he is. Whether the shot share comes back is the more important question, and it depends on what's in front of him.
